statement: Mitochondrial inner-membrane cristae are shaped functional structures: their junction necks are held by the MICOS complex and ATP synthase dimerizes along the curved cristae rims, generating the curvature that packs ETC machinery and maximizes proton-motive-force-generating surface area.

provenance.primary: Cogliati, Enriquez & Scorrano — cristae shape & OXPHOS efficiency (Trends Biochem Sci 2016); MICOS/ATP-synthase-dimer literature

confidence_notes: Established cell biology; the link cristae-density <-> capacity is robust, the in-vivo dynamics of remodeling are an active area.

statement: Complex I is a principal site of mitochondrial ROS production, especially via reverse electron transport (RET) when the proton-motive force is high and the CoQ pool is reduced (e.g. succinate accumulation after ischemia drives the RET-ROS burst of reperfusion injury).
effect_size: Mechanistic (RET as a major superoxide source)

provenance.primary: Chouchani et al. — Ischaemic accumulation of succinate controls reperfusion injury through ROS, Nature 2014

confidence_notes: RET as a dominant physiological ROS source is well supported in heart I/R; relative contribution across tissues/conditions still studied.

statement: Human mtDNA is a ~16.5 kb circular genome encoding 37 genes (13 ETC protein subunits, 22 tRNAs, 2 rRNAs); the other ~1,500 mitochondrial proteins are nuclear-encoded and imported, so the organelle runs on a two-genome collaboration requiring mito-nuclear coordination.

provenance.primary: Anderson et al. — Sequence and organization of the human mitochondrial genome, Nature 1981; MitoCarta inventory (Calvo/Mootha)

confidence_notes: Settled fact; the ~1,500 figure tracks MitoCarta updates.

statement: mtDNA is maternally inherited; cells carry hundreds-to-thousands of copies that can be a mix of wild-type and mutant (heteroplasmy); a mutant load usually causes no phenotype until it crosses a tissue-specific threshold (~60-80% mutant), beyond which the most energy-demanding tissues fail first.

provenance.primary: Wallace, D. C. — mtDNA, heteroplasmy and the threshold effect (Annu Rev Genet 2005; Science 1999)

confidence_notes: Uncontested foundation of mitochondrial medicine; threshold value varies by mutation and tissue energy demand.

statement: PINK1/Parkin mitophagy uses inner-membrane potential as the honesty signal: PINK1 is imported and degraded in healthy (polarized) mitochondria, but when membrane potential collapses, PINK1 accumulates on the outer membrane, recruits/activates Parkin, which ubiquitinates the organelle for selective autophagic destruction.

provenance.primary: Narendra, Tanaka, Suen & Youle — Parkin recruited selectively to impaired mitochondria, J Cell Biol 2008; Narendra et al. PLoS Biol 2010 (PINK1)

confidence_notes: Established; PINK1/Parkin-independent routes (BNIP3, NIX, FUNDC1) also exist. Loss-of-function mutations cause early-onset Parkinson's.

statement: Loss-of-function mutations in PINK1 and PARKIN (PARK2) cause autosomal-recessive early-onset Parkinson's disease, implicating failed mitochondrial quality control (mitophagy) in dopaminergic neurodegeneration.

provenance.primary: Kitada et al. Nature 1998 (Parkin); Valente et al. Science 2004 (PINK1)

confidence_notes: Monogenic causation is solid for these rare familial forms; their relevance to common sporadic PD is suggestive, not proven.

statement: PGC-1alpha is the master transcriptional co-activator of mitochondrial biogenesis; the four classic good-stress signals (rising AMP:ATP via AMPK, Ca2+ via CaMK, transient ROS, and NAD+/SIRT1) all converge on it to induce NRF1/2, ERRalpha and TFAM, which build new ETC complexes and replicate mtDNA. This convergence is why exercise, fasting, cold and CR share a final common biogenesis pathway.

provenance.primary: Wu et al. Cell 1999; Puigserver & Spiegelman Endocr Rev 2003; Lin, Handschin & Spiegelman Cell Metab 2005

confidence_notes: Established as the central node; biogenesis is multi-regulator and PGC-1a is necessary-but-not-sole in some contexts.

statement: Mitochondria continuously fuse (MFN1/2 outer, OPA1 inner; mixes contents, dilutes damage, favored under nutrient scarcity) and divide (DRP1; segregates damaged units for mitophagy, enables distribution/division); aging and metabolic disease skew toward chronic fragmentation, and MFN2 (CMT2A) / OPA1 (dominant optic atrophy) mutations prove the machinery is essential.
population: Mammalian cell biology + human dynamics-gene disease

provenance.primary: Chan, D. C. — Mitochondrial dynamics and its involvement in disease, Annu Rev Pathol 2020; Youle & van der Bliek Science 2012

confidence_notes: Molecular biology established; 'improve your fission-fusion balance' as a consumer protocol does not exist independent of exercise/fasting.

statement: The naive free-radical/oxidative-damage theory of aging is mostly resolved against itself: large antioxidant-supplement RCTs (vitamin E, beta-carotene, vitamin A) show no mortality benefit and some harm; supplemental vitamin C+E blunts the mitochondrial-biogenesis adaptation to exercise; and genetically boosting most antioxidant defenses does not extend mouse lifespan as predicted.
effect_size: Antioxidant RCTs null-to-harmful; vit C+E reduce training adaptation
population: Human RCT meta-analyses + human exercise trials + mouse genetics

provenance.primary: Bjelakovic et al. JAMA 2007 (antioxidant mortality meta); Ristow et al. PNAS 2009 (antioxidants blunt exercise)

confidence_notes: The NAIVE damage/antioxidant form is refuted; ROS-as-damage still occurs - the correction is that ROS are also required signals (mitohormesis).

statement: Mitohormesis: a transient, sub-damaging burst of mitochondrial ROS is an adaptive signal that activates NRF2 (endogenous antioxidant/phase-II program) and PGC-1alpha (biogenesis), making the system net-stronger - a biphasic dose-response. Transient mitochondrial ROS is the shared engine under exercise, fasting, cold, and xenohormetic polyphenols.

provenance.primary: Ristow, M. & Schmeisser, K. — Mitohormesis: promoting health and lifespan by increased ROS, Dose-Response 2014; Ristow PNAS 2009

confidence_notes: Molecular mechanism well supported; the hormesis frame becomes unfalsifiable if used to retro-explain any result (see hormesis-unifying-frame).

statement: Mitochondrial function declines with age across tissues (oxidative capacity, membrane potential, biogenesis/PGC-1a signaling, mitophagy, supercomplex organization, NAD+ availability) - a robust phenomenon and a named Hallmark of Aging (antagonistic category).

provenance.primary: Lopez-Otin et al. Hallmarks of Aging, Cell 2013/2023; Sun, Youle & Finkel Mol Cell 2016

confidence_notes: The decline as a phenomenon is solid; whether it is a DRIVER of aging or a downstream readout is open (see conflict-mtdna-mutation-causality).

statement: Somatic mtDNA mutations accumulate and clonally expand with age (solid); the POLG mutator mouse ages prematurely (solid) but at mutation loads far above human levels and via apoptosis rather than ROS damage; whether somatic mtDNA mutation CAUSES normal human aging remains contested/open.
effect_size: Mutator-mouse premature aging at supraphysiologic loads; causality in normal aging unresolved

provenance.primary: Trifunovic et al. Nature 2004; Kujoth et al. Science 2005 (apoptosis not ROS)

confidence_notes: Phenomenon solid, causal role in NORMAL human aging open - a flagship example of a robust phenomenon with unresolved causality.

statement: Aerobic/Zone-2 + HIIT endurance training is the strongest, best-evidenced mitochondrial lever: it drives PGC-1a biogenesis (Holloszy 1967: ~doubles mitochondrial enzyme content), and VO2max - which physiologically IS integrated mitochondrial capacity - is the strongest mortality predictor in preventive medicine.
effect_size: Endurance training ~doubles mito enzyme content; VO2max strongest mortality predictor (cohort)

provenance.primary: Holloszy J Biol Chem 1967; Mandsager et al. JAMA Netw Open 2018 (CRF & mortality)

confidence_notes: Biogenesis mechanism certain; VO2max-mortality link is cohort/meta (cannot randomize decades of fitness; partial reverse causation). Zone-2-uniquely-optimal is over-extrapolated.

statement: Red/near-infrared light (~660-850 nm) is absorbed by cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) and can increase its activity in vitro/animal models (photobiomodulation); human outcome data are small, heterogeneous and indication-specific (skin, some muscle recovery, retinal), not a validated general mitochondrial booster.
effect_size: Real Cx IV photochemistry; human outcomes small/narrow

provenance.primary: Hamblin, M. R. — Mechanisms and mitochondrial redox signaling in photobiomodulation, Photochem Photobiol 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: deep-dive levers table (PBM honest narrow evidence)

confidence_notes: Mechanism plausible/real; graded promising-but-thin, not established for general use. Distinct from Kruse's broader speculative light claims.

statement: CoQ10/ubiquinol has a positive hard-endpoint RCT in moderate-severe heart failure (Q-SYMBIO: 300 mg/d ~halved MACE and all-cause mortality over 2 years) and is genuinely therapeutic in primary CoQ10 deficiency; but in healthy people it shows no demonstrated benefit and statin-myalgia RCTs are mostly null.
effect_size: Q-SYMBIO HR ~0.5 for MACE/mortality in HF; null for statin myalgia; no benefit in healthy

provenance.primary: Mortensen et al. — Q-SYMBIO, JACC Heart Failure 2014 (PMID 25282031)

confidence_notes: Strongest outcome evidence of any supplement in this chapter, but context-specific (HF/deficiency); do not generalize to healthy people.

statement: Urolithin A (Mitopure) is a genuine, replicated mitophagy inducer in cells and animals; human RCTs (Andreux 2019 first-in-human safety/molecular signature; Singh 2022 older adults; Liu 2022 middle-aged) show small, mostly-surrogate effects (muscle endurance, mitochondrial gene expression, ~+12% strength), missed some primary endpoints (6-min walk), have no hard endpoints, and are industry (Amazentis)-funded.
effect_size: Modest/surrogate: muscle endurance + mito gene expression; ~+12% strength (Liu); no hard endpoints

provenance.primary: Andreux et al. Nat Metab 2019; Singh et al. JAMA Netw Open 2022 (PMID 35050355); Liu et al. Cell Rep Med 2022 (PMID 35584623)
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed urolithin A trials + deep-dive supplement section

confidence_notes: Best-evidenced 'mitophagy supplement' but mechanism != outcome: real mechanism, modest surrogate effects, no hard endpoints, all sponsor-funded. Promising, not proven.

statement: MitoQ (CoQ conjugated to a triphenylphosphonium cation that concentrates it ~hundredfold in the mitochondrial matrix; developed by Michael P. Murphy & Robin Smith) improved endothelial function (FMD ~42%) in older adults in one RCT (Rossman 2018) but exercise/redox trials are inconsistent (some peak-power benefit, no change in mitochondrial content); as a targeted antioxidant it risks blunting training adaptation.
effect_size: FMD +~42% (Rossman, older adults); exercise outcomes inconsistent
population: Healthy older adults (Rossman 2018); trained cyclists/older adults (exercise trials)

provenance.primary: Rossman et al. — Chronic MitoQ improves vascular function in healthy older adults, Hypertension 2018 (PMID 29661838)
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed MitoQ trials + deep-dive supplement section

confidence_notes: Elegant targeting, one real endothelial signal, inconsistent elsewhere; antioxidant-blunting concern applies. Unproven for general use.

statement: PQQ (pyrroloquinoline quinone) is marketed as a PGC-1alpha/mitochondrial-biogenesis activator, but the supporting human trials are small, frequently industry-funded, and report inconsistent surrogate endpoints (cognition scores, mitochondrial biomarkers, modest aerobic markers in untrained men); the biogenesis claim is largely preclinical.
effect_size: Small/inconsistent surrogate effects; biogenesis claim mostly preclinical
population: Small human trials (healthy volunteers, untrained men, elderly)

provenance.primary: Hwang et al. J Am Coll Nutr 2020 (PMID 31860387, aerobic/biogenesis markers); Itoh et al. cognition trials
provenance.surfaced_via: PubMed PQQ randomized + deep-dive supplement section

confidence_notes: Weak tier; not established. Rides mitochondrial-biogenesis prestige past the human data.

statement: Primary (inherited) mitochondrial diseases - the most common inherited metabolic disorders (~1 in 4,300), caused by mtDNA (maternal, heteroplasmic) or nuclear-gene mutations - selectively damage the most energy-demanding post-mitotic tissues first (brain, heart, muscle, retina, cochlea), and even in these defined-lesion patients the 'mitochondrial cocktail' supplements have modest-to-weak evidence and no cure.
effect_size: Prevalence ~1/4300; tissue-selective by energy demand; supplement cocktails weak
population: Human mitochondrial-disease patients (MELAS, MERRF, Leigh, LHON, Kearns-Sayre)

provenance.primary: Gorman et al. — Mitochondrial diseases, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2016; Pfeffer et al. Cochrane 2012 (treatment for mito disorders)

confidence_notes: Tissue-selectivity is the clinical proof of the master-variable thesis; weak supplement evidence even here lowers the prior for healthy-person 'optimization'.
